tool_summary: Crystal's package manager. Resolves and installs dependencies declared in shard.yml. Installed shards' code is compiled and executed as part of any subsequent `crystal build`/`crystal run`/`shards build`.
platform_notes: shards behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS. Notable as the package manager of commandant.cr's own ecosystem.

rules.description: Resolves and fetches dependencies declared in shard.yml. Unlike gem/npm, shards itself does not execute install-time build scripts, but fetched source will be compiled and executed the next time the project is built or run, with the invoking user's privileges at that point.
rules.reversible_note: Fetched dependencies can be removed, but if a subsequent build/run has already compiled and executed the fetched code, that execution is not undone.

rules.description: Compiles the project (and its dependencies) into a binary. Crystal macros run at compile time, meaning dependency code can execute during the build itself, not only when the resulting binary is later run.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on what dependency macros or the resulting binary do, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: Manages Crystal project dependencies. Read-only subcommands (list, outdated, check) do not fetch, compile, or execute dependency code. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future shards subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
